extracted.intended_audience: literary critics and periodical reviewers (especially of poetry); students of literary criticism; poets interested in critical standards
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and practical guidelines for fairly and philosophically judging poetry and for running periodical reviews — how to ground criticism in explicit principles, use evidence, avoid personal abuse, and assess poetic style and defects. Focuses especially on reviewing Wordsworth and on periodical criticism practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce and establish critical principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic announces and endeavours to establish the principles which he holds for the foundation of poetry in general, with the specification of these in their application to the different classes of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before passing judgment, prepare and state your canons of criticism (theory of poetry) and then apply those canons specifically to the work under review so readers can judge your consistency and basis for praise or condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularize evidence and show recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed to particularize the most striking passages to which he deems [the principles] applicable, faithfully noticing the frequent or infrequent recurrence of similar merits or defects, and as faithfully distinguishing what is characteristic from what is accidental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support general claims by quoting specific passages; note how often such features occur across the work; distinguish characteristic traits of the author/poem from incidental lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make premises explicit and deductions legitimate
rubrics_metrics.description: If his premises be rational, his deductions legitimate, and his conclusions justly applied, the reader ... may adopt his judgment in the light of judgment and in the independence of free-agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your argument is logically coherent: state premises, derive conclusions transparently, and apply them properly. When you err, do so openly so others can detect and correct errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal allusions and private-knowledge attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as the critic betrays, that he knows more of his author, than the author’s publications could have told him; ... his censure instantly becomes personal injury, his sarcasms personal insults. He ceases to be a critic ... and takes on him the most contemptible character ... a gossip, backbiter, and pasquillant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit criticism to what is demonstrable from the published work; do not introduce private details or insinuations drawn from knowledge outside the text; personal malice transforms critique into abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the author only as the impersonation of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Every censure, every sarcasm respecting a publication which the critic, with the criticised work before him, can make good, is the critic’s right. The writer is authorized to reply, but not to complain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame censure as critique of the published work; avoid ad hominem attacks. The author may respond, but public complaint against legitimate textual criticism is unwarranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique works susceptible to argumentative criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Review those books only, which are susceptible and deserving of argumentative criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select for review works that merit reasoned argument rather than brief denunciation; leave trash or mediocrity to sink into oblivion except when larger argument is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reviewing trivial works for sale or malice
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjecting to criticism works neither indecent nor immoral, yet of such trifling importance even in point of size and ... so devoid of all merit, as must excite ... suspicion, either that dislike or vindictive feelings were at work; or that there was a cold prudential pre-determination to increase the sale of the review by flattering the malignant passions of human nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not devote argumentative energy to inconsequential pamphlets or tiny works merely to stir controversy or boost circulation; this undermines the reviewer’s integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground criticism in universal morals and philosophic reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounding this code on the two-fold basis of universal morals and philosophic reason, independent of all foreseen application to particular works and authors, they obtain the right to speak each as the representative of their body corporate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers claim institutional authority, adopt an explicit constitution or code grounded on broadly defensible moral and rational principles and pledge to judge according to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh words according to intended effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic must know, what effect it is his object to produce; and with a view to this effect must he weigh his words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose tone and language deliberately to achieve a known rhetorical aim; severity, irony, or mildness are tactical choices that should be consciously made, not accidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not revive old juvenile works to attack author
rubrics_metrics.description: No ... re-commitment (for new trial) of juvenile performances, that were published, perhaps forgotten, many years before the commencement of the review: since for the forcing back of such works to public notice no motives are easily assignable, but such as are furnished to the critic by his own personal malignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dredging up youthful writings long forgotten to embarrass or vilify an author; historical context matters and revenge-motivated resurfacing is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid substitution of assertion for argument
rubrics_metrics.description: I am referring to the substitution of assertion for argument; to the frequency of arbitrary and sometimes petulant verdicts, not seldom unsupported even by a single quotation from the work condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make large claims about a work without argument or textual evidence; support verdicts with quotations and reasoned explanation rather than bald assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support critical claims with quotations and general grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where [quotations] are not the case, the extracts are too often made without reference to any general grounds or rules from which the faultiness ... may be deduced; and without any attempt to show, that the qualities are attributable to the passage extracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When quoting passages, connect them to stated critical principles; show how the extract exemplifies the fault or merit you attribute, rather than using quotes as rhetorical ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid national party bias or personal predilection
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting aside the too manifest and too frequent interference of national party, and even personal predilection or aversion; and reserving for deeper feelings those worse and more criminal intrusions ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for objectivity; do not let nationalistic, political, or personal loyalties distort assessments of literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish characteristic features from accidental ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Faithfully distinguishing what is characteristic from what is accidental, or a mere flagging of the wing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an author's style or recurring defects, determine whether a feature is a stable, defining trait or a sporadic lapse; this affects remedial critique and overall judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess pervasiveness and separability of defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Let it likewise be shown, how far the influence has acted; whether diffusively, or only by starts; whether the number and importance of the poems and passages thus infected be great or trifling compared with the sound portion; and lastly, whether they are inwoven into the texture of his works, or are loose and separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the scope of any alleged theoretical or stylistic error: is it widespread and structural, or limited and removable? This moderates condemnation and indicates remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge suitability of character and mode to poetic aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether this be a character appropriate to a lofty didactick poem, is perhaps questionable. It presents a fair subject for controversy; and the question is to be determined by the congruity or incongruity of such a character with what shall be proved to be the essential constituents of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether characters, narrative modes, or subject-matter cohere with the intended genre and dignity of the poem; incongruous choices require justification or critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: The poet should select the most dignified or happiest attitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The office and duty of the poet is to select the most dignified as well as 'The gayest, happiest attitude of things.' The reverse ... is the appropriate business of burlesque and travesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets aiming at loftiness should choose elevated, noble perspectives; persistent burlesque or low treatment is appropriate only to genres that explicitly demand it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconstancy of style and abrupt transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The inconstancy of the style ... sudden and unprepared transitions from lines or sentences of peculiar felicity ... to a style, not only unimpassioned but undistinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a coherent stylistic level within a work; prepare transitions so that elevated poetic passages do not sink abruptly into neutral prose, which creates anticlimax or stylistic dissonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect distinctions among poetic, prose, and neutral diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide language into three species; first, that which is peculiar to poetry; second, that which is only proper in prose; and third, the neutral or common to both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and use appropriately poetic diction versus prose diction; blending requires skill and justification. Where poetry demands raised diction, adjust surrounding language to support it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise lower tints to support commanding poetic colours
rubrics_metrics.description: The business of the writer ... is so to raise the lower and neutral tints, that what in a different style would be the commanding colours, are here used as the means of that gentle degradation requisite in order to produce the effect of a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inserting striking poetic lines, elevate surrounding language so the striking lines integrate harmoniously rather than startling by contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate diction for naturalness and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are those words in those places commonly employed in real life to express the same thought or outward thing? Are they the style used in the ordinary intercourse of spoken words? No! nor are the modes of connections; and still less the breaks and transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether unusual or polysyllabic words serve precision and poetic purpose, or whether they create affectation or unintelligibility; consider naturalness relative to poetic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow poetic grammatical peculiarities when justified
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a peculiarity in the frequent use of the asymartaeton ... and not less in the construction of words by apposition ('to him, a youth').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual grammatical constructions may be defensible artistic choices—note and evaluate them, but do not dismiss them out of hand if they enhance poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of critics who judge before reading
rubrics_metrics.description: I have met with such extracts ... as led me to imagine, that the reviewer, having written his critique before he had read the work, had then pricked with a pin for passages, wherewith to illustrate the various branches of his preconceived opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure thorough reading before forming judgments; avoid hunting for pre-selected examples to confirm an a priori verdict.
